title: a second ground loop exits quietly, --force replaces it, and the ground-loop lock path carries the cairn instance
intention: A ground loop that finds a live one exits 0 quietly and leaves it running; --force kills the old one and takes the claim; the ground loop's lock path carries the cairn instance. The bus (clause 1 for bus.lock) and shim naming (<device>_1) are separate tickets, RULE 1.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendell: live box: bus.lock held=True and ground_loop run.lock held=True (singleton.held); one bus launcher+child pair (1648->16184) and one ground_loop shim+child pair (23396->4904), no duplicates; the bus child 16184 owns conhost 16980, the ground_loop child 4904 none seen
traces_to: Law 1 (one claim tool, not one per site); Law 4 (the kernel lock, not a convention); Law 7 (the loser refuses loudly); the orchestrator's note that I-the-command-lazy-inits-the-system.md rejects a host-local lock with no instance name.
how: Census first: for ground_loop, bus, rack and a cc name on the bus, record what a spin-up does when a live copy exists. Then close each gap with the cairn/tools/base/singleton.py claim, keyed by cairn instance, and prove each by a second claimant that exits.

clauses.claim: a second ground loop started while the first is live exits 0 with nothing on stdout or stderr and leaves the first running; with --force it kills the old one and holds the claim
the ground loop's lock path contains the cairn instance segment (devices/cairn/0/...), not a host-global path

decisions.text: D1: --force is guard.force_claim (kills the record's pid, retries the claim); the runner _claim returns (claim, exit_code); the loser's exit is 0 and silent; a failed --force is loud, exit 3 (EXIT_FORCE_FAILED).

D2: ground_loop's own proof moves with it: test_the_doors_loser_exits_zero_and_says_nothing replaces the exit-3 tooth (PROVES bae622881f03 clause 7), and the no-takeover tooth now expects exit 0 and silence.
D3: one new proof, one tooth per clause.

measured.saw: live box: bus.lock held=True and ground_loop run.lock held=True (singleton.held); one bus launcher+child pair (1648->16184) and one ground_loop shim+child pair (23396->4904), no duplicates; the bus child 16184 owns conhost 16980, the ground_loop child 4904 none seen
measured.how: singleton.held over every *.lock under ~/.cairn, plus Get-CimInstance Win32_Process, read only (nothing spawned)

measured.saw: singleton.py locks on nt with msvcrt.locking; bus/server.py _lock() also does, with its own claim() beside it rather than singleton.claim; ground_loop/guard.py claims through singleton.claim and its __main__ catches ClaimRefused

NOT censused: what a second bus or ground_loop start prints and exits with on nt; whether rack (a roster in cairn/tools/rack/rack.py, no process) needs a claim; whether the bus refuses a second connection under a live device name (grep for duplicate-name handling in bus/*.py and bus_client/*.py found none)
measured.how: grep; the run itself would spawn processes, HYPOTHESIS that bus server.py exits EXIT_HELD (line 936) as its message says

measured.saw: Akien answered Q#93: the ticket's 'loudly' was wrong for a second singleton copy: 'spinning up a second ground loop should see the first, and that it's fine, and exit quietly'; '--force, which means kill the old one'; 'i have no recollection why it says loudly'. Naming: two zeros could not be routed, so 'the launcher has to ask the shim to create the instance ... it's the shim's job to say we have a cc_0 instance, so I'll launch it with cc_1'. Some things (embeddings generator) may run several instances, so singleton-ness is per component, not universal.
